newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Pacific Ports set for strong debut.
newsitem.headline: HK's Pacific Ports set for strong debut.

text.p: Shares of Pacific Ports Co Ltd, the port operating arm of Fairyoung Holdings Ltd, are poised for a strong market debut on Friday, analysts said.

Analysts said anticipation that the company will benefit from the partial renewal of direct shipping links between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland, plus a grey market price of about HK$3.65 per share, were expected to give the stock good support.

"Those companies related to port operations in southern China are likely to enjoy better growth potential in wake of the direct shipping links," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.

Pacific Ports is engaged in investment in and development, operation and management of terminals in seaports and riverports in Asia. It holds development rights for five port infrastructure projects in Xiamen in China's Fujian Province and in Nanjing and Suzhou in Jiangsu province.

Direct shipping links across the Taiwan Strait were reopened this month after a 48-year hiatus between Xiamen and Taiwan's Kaohsiung, although Taipei currently allows only transshipment of Chinese goods headed for third countries.

Pacific Ports offered 200 million shares at HK$3.09 each in its flotation, of which 160 million shares were placed with institutional and professional investors and 40 million shares were opened for public offering in Hong Kong.
The public portion of the offer was 141 times subscribed.
"We expect strong overseas demand for the stock because it will be the first pure ports play in the market," said a sales director at a European brokerage.
Analysts said the company's prospect was also seen to be optimistic given strong demand for good quality ports for sustained export growth in China.
Pacific Ports said it is also exploring other port investment opportunities throughout Asia.

The company said the net proceeds raised from the issue would be about HK$583 million, of which HK$460 million would be used to invest in its ports and related projects in China over the next three years. The rest would be used as working capital.
